---
name: reindex-definitionally-then-rfl
description: Before transporting a kernel/equalizer along an index bijection, arrange the reindexed data to be definitionally the original at the relabelled index — then the intertwining lemma does not exist.
metadata:
  type: project
---

Transporting a submodule-as-kernel along an index equivalence looks like it needs an
intertwining lemma for each arrow. It usually does not. Define the reindexed datum so its
components are *definitionally* the original at the relabelled index (`pieces j :=
D.pieces (e j)`); then for a pair-indexed structure, reindexing acts **diagonally**, so
the arrow at `(i,j)` is `rfl`-equal to the original at `(e i, e j)` and every comparison
collapses. In AJCR this turned a predicted ~100 lines into zero (retracted in c71a8f684)
and later made all seven certificate clauses transport in `DivisorFamilyAffCompare.lean`.

Two spellings that matter when it is not quite free:
- Use `LinearEquiv.piCongrLeft` in its **`symm`** direction — `(piCongrLeft φ e).symm g j =
  g (e j)` evaluates cast-free, while the forward direction carries an `Eq.mpr` you then
  fight.
- `Submodule.comap`/`map` equalities may fail to elaborate where the membership `iff` form
  succeeds, when instance search cannot unfold through the reindexed carrier.

Also: `V ⊓ V = V` for `Opens` is `inf_idem`, **propositional not definitional**, so
`Γ(X, V ⊓ V)` and `Γ(X, V)` are different types and need a real algebra equivalence. And
`Ideal.map` takes the `RingHom` coercion of an `AlgEquiv`, which `rw` will not match
against the `AlgEquiv` application — state the helper lemma in both coercions.

**Why:** the expensive mistake is reaching for the transport machinery before checking
whether the definitional arrangement is available.

**How to apply:** when facing an index relabelling, first try to make the data defeq at
the relabelled index and test with `rfl`. Only build transport lemmas for what genuinely
changes type.
